title: per-request-quality-signal-experiment-orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an experiment orchestration hub that lets product and platform engineers define A/B and canary experiments driven by per-request quality signals (e.g., answer correctness, hallucination score, latency-sensitive SLOs). The hub will coordinate traffic splits, shadow mirroring, continuous statistical checks, and automated rollback when pre-specified guardrails are breached. It integrates with Redwood Console for visualization and with the runtime for traffic routing and KV cache handling.

Scope:
- Experiment authoring UX (experiment definition, variant bindings, cohort selectors) in Console.
- Deterministic ramp schedules and exposure budgets with per-cohort control.
- Real-time metric ingestion and sequential statistical tests (frequentist and optional Bayesian checks).
- Shadow traffic pipeline for warm-start evaluation without user exposure.
- Auto-rollback and soft-fail strategies (model fallback, reduced exposure, traffic draining).
- Audit logs, experiment lineage, and PRD/metadata persisted for compliance.

Out of scope for initial iteration: long-running multi-month experiments, built-in metric ingestion from third-party vendors (we will provide connectors later).

Success metrics: percentage reduction in manual rollback incidents for model rollouts, time-to-detect regressions, and developer satisfaction survey for experiment UX.
acceptance_criteria: Console: users can create an experiment with two model variants, define cohorts, and schedule a deterministic ramp (0->10->50->100%).
Runtime: routing policy supports per-request decisions based on cohort and produces mirrored shadow copies to a non-production evaluation pipeline.
Telemetry: per-variant metrics emitted (latency, token cost, quality signal) with 1s ingestion latency for realtime checks.
Checks: sequential hypothesis test runs continuously and triggers a rollback action when a metric breach persists beyond N windows.
Rollback actions: automatic fallback to baseline variant, annotation in audit log, and a Console notification sent to configured owners.
Docs: PRD, runbook, and a short how-to guide published in the internal docs site with example experiment templates.
notes: Design decision 2026-01-22: use a hybrid testing approach — default to Wald sequential probability ratio tests for simple thresholds and provide an opt-in Bayesian posterior-check mode for teams that want richer uncertainty modeling.
Trade-off: aggressive sequential tests reduce time-to-detect but increase false positives. We'll expose sensitivity knobs and recommend pre-computed sample sizes for expected effect sizes.
Runtime constraint: KV cache warming can bias early quality metrics. We will include a 'warm-up' flag that excludes the first X requests from metric windows per variant.

Integrations: Console feature flag will surface experiment health and provide one-click rollback. Instrumentation will hook into existing tracing (X-Request-ID) and per-request metadata tags (experiment_id, variant_id).
Security/compliance: experiments produce audit logs with requester, experiment config, and variant commits; retention follows platform policy (90 days by default).
